---
title: "Rolling Hash"
description: "A mathematical algorithm explained in plain English and with an explicit numerical substitution."
---

## Start with a specific question

**LeetCode 28 — Find the Index of the First Occurrence in a String (Rabin–Karp variant).** We will reason from a very small example rather than introduce a complicated notation first.

## What the obvious approach overlooks

Recompute the numeric fingerprint of each length-m substring from scratch, even though adjacent substrings share m−1 characters.

## One simple idea

Update a hash by removing the outgoing symbol's contribution, shifting by the base and adding the new symbol. Check actual characters when hashes match.

Before reading symbols, explain the intended operation aloud. If you can say which information is saved and which work is avoided, you have the core intuition.

## Formula and immediate translation

$$
H_{i+1}=(B(H_i-c_iB^{m-1})+c_{i+m})\bmod M
$$

**Symbols and notation:** H_i is the hash of the length-m window starting at i; B is the alphabet base, M modulus, c_i outgoing encoded character, c_(i+m) incoming encoded character.

**Insert actual numbers:** For digits '1234', window size m=3, base B=10 and a large modulus M>1000, H₀=123. Remove outgoing 1×100 to get 23, shift by 10 to 230 and add incoming 4: H₁=234, matching substring '234'.

This numerical calculation is essential: the expression must mean the same thing when evaluated by hand and when written in code.

## Why the mathematics leads to an algorithm

The polynomial hash is a base-B positional number. Adjacent windows differ by one removed digit, multiplication by B, and one appended digit, so the update represents the next window.

This argument is the bridge between 'the equation looks plausible' and 'the result is correct for all inputs satisfying the assumptions'.

## Make the idea executable

The [original algorithm examples](../examples/patterns.mjs) provide a small runnable related operation:

~~~js
import { kmpFind } from '../examples/patterns.mjs';

console.log(kmpFind('ababcabc','abc'));
~~~

Run from a saved `.mjs` file inside this topic directory. The exported operation is tested with Node's standard test runner. Some examples illustrate a prerequisite rather than the entire specialised algorithm; in that case, the mathematical model above remains the definition of the full task.

## Complexity and correctness boundaries

**Work bound:** O(n+m) expected matching with rolling updates and verification as needed; worst-case can approach O(nm) under adversarial collisions.

**Counterexample or limitation:** Hashes can collide: matching hash values do NOT prove strings equal. Modulo with negative intermediates requires normalisation in some languages.

Always declare the input domain first. For example, a modulus must be positive, a probability denominator nonzero and a character indexing convention fixed. Many seemingly clever solutions fail because these conditions were never stated.
